To assemble a sample, RiboPilot compares its reads with known ribosomal
sequences from related organisms: a reference database. A new project has no
usable database until you build one, for each group of related samples, in the
app's **Reference** step. You do not need to find or format any sequences
yourself, and a database is reused by every later project on that group.

# The Reference step

The Reference step comes between the **Taxonomy** and **Assemble** steps. Set
up a database for every group before you assemble.

Once your samples' taxonomy is assigned, open the Reference step and press
**Propose groups**. RiboPilot looks at each sample's lineage and groups samples
that can share one reference database, using how many ribosomal sequences
GenBank holds for each candidate group: a group needs at least 1,000 GenBank
records to make a useful reference, and RiboPilot picks the narrowest group
(family, order, class, and so on) that clears that bar. If that group holds more
than 25,000 records, the proposal says so in red: its database takes longer to
build, and you can narrow it later with **Change which clade this group uses**.
Samples from very different parts of the tree end up in different groups, each
with its own database.

Each row is one proposed group. The **Status** column says where that group
stands ("Needs a database", "Building", "Ready", "Build failed", or "Left on
current database"), and the rest of the row shows the clade, how many of your
samples it covers, and how many GenBank records back it up.

## Setting a group up

The link at the right-hand end of each row says what that group needs: **Set up
database**, **Try again**, or **Change**. Click it and you are offered four
choices:

- **Download sequences from GenBank.** The normal choice. Opens a run window
  like the one in the Assemble step; press **Run from App**. When the build
  finishes, RiboPilot points the group's unlocked samples at the new database.
  A database that already exists in your reference folder is used right away,
  with no new build.
- **Use a database I already have.** Points the group at a database built
  earlier, in this project or by someone else sharing the reference folder.
- **Change which clade this group uses.** Lists the group's lineage from the
  broadest rank to the narrowest. Pick another rank to widen or narrow the
  group, or search for another clade. Samples the new clade does not cover are
  split off into a group of their own. Clicking the group's **Clade** cell
  opens the same window.
- **Leave these samples on their current database.** Nothing is built. Use it
  only when you have already set a database in these samples' **Assembly
  Options** yourself.

To handle several groups at once, tick their rows first, then click the link on
any one of them. The clade option is offered only for a single group.

If you press **Update** in the Assemble step while some groups have no
database, RiboPilot warns you but goes ahead, and those samples fail.

# The reference folder

Built databases live in a **reference folder** that is shared across projects:
one clade database, built once, is reused by every project that needs that clade,
and if the folder is on a shared drive, by everyone in your lab. You can set it in
the Reference step with the **Settings** button (which also lets you adjust the
minimum and maximum record counts the grouping step uses), or when you create a
project:

```r
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path       = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path  = "~/my_reads",
  ref_dir    = "~/ribopilot_refs"
)
```

If you do not set a folder, RiboPilot uses a folder in your home directory;
`RiboPilot::ribopilot_ref_dir()` prints it. On a cluster, move it off your home
directory: see [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html).

# The 5.8S gene

GenBank rarely stores 5.8S on its own; it is usually inside ITS records. That
is fine: RiboPilot still recovers the 5.8S region from the full repeat.
